\section{Introduction}

A central goal of computational complexity theory is to prove unconditional lower
bounds: to show that certain functions cannot be computed by small or shallow
devices, regardless of cleverness. Boolean circuits are the canonical
non-uniform model. Proving super-polynomial circuit lower bounds for an explicit
function in $NP$ would separate $P$ from $NP$; this remains out of reach.

\emph{Monotone} circuits---those built from AND and OR gates only, with no
NOT---are a restricted but natural and powerful model, because they exactly
capture the monotone Boolean functions, which include many fundamental graph and
combinatorial properties. Razborov's landmark theorem (1985) established that
monotone circuits for $k$-CLIQUE require \emph{exponential} size. The
complementary Karchmer--Wigderson correspondence equates minimal circuit depth
with the deterministic communication complexity of an associated two-player
relation.

\subsection{Contributions}
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\arabic*)]
  \item A generic inductive definition of monotone circuits over an arbitrary
  index type, with evaluation, size, depth, and variable-set semantics.
  \item Four structural theorems: monotonicity of computed functions, locality,
  relevance implies occurrence, and the variable-count size bound.
  \item The relevant-variable size lower bound.
  \item A formalization of CLIQUE in the edge-variable model, its monotonicity,
  and a quadratic ($\binom{m}{2}$) monotone size lower bound for $2$-CLIQUE.
  \item A precise statement and proof sketch of the Karchmer--Wigderson forward
  direction and a roadmap to the converse, Razborov's method, and separation.
\end{enumerate}

\section{Monotone circuits: definitions}

Throughout, $\iota$ is an arbitrary type of variable indices, and an \emph{input
assignment} is a function $x : \iota \to \Bool$.

\begin{definition}[Monotone circuit]
The type $\MCircuit(\iota)$ of monotone Boolean circuits over $\iota$ is generated
inductively by: $\mathrm{var}(i)$ for $i:\iota$ (an input leaf); $\top$ (the
constant $\true$); $\bot$ (the constant $\false$); $\mathrm{and}(a,b)$ (an AND
gate); and $\mathrm{or}(a,b)$ (an OR gate).
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Evaluation]
The value $\eval(C,x):\Bool$ is defined recursively by
$\eval(\mathrm{var}\,i,x)=x_i$, $\eval(\top,x)=\true$, $\eval(\bot,x)=\false$,
$\eval(\mathrm{and}(a,b),x)=\eval(a,x)\mathbin{\&\&}\eval(b,x)$, and
$\eval(\mathrm{or}(a,b),x)=\eval(a,x)\mathbin{||}\eval(b,x)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Size]
$\size(\mathrm{var}\,i)=\size(\top)=\size(\bot)=1$, and
$\size(\mathrm{and}(a,b))=\size(\mathrm{or}(a,b))=\size(a)+\size(b)+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Depth]
$\depth$ of a leaf or constant is $0$, and
$\depth(\mathrm{and}(a,b))=\depth(\mathrm{or}(a,b))=\max(\depth(a),\depth(b))+1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Variables read]
Assuming decidable equality on $\iota$,
$\vars(\mathrm{var}\,i)=\{i\}$, $\vars(\top)=\vars(\bot)=\emptyset$, and
$\vars(\mathrm{and}(a,b))=\vars(\mathrm{or}(a,b))=\vars(a)\cup\vars(b)$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Pointwise order]
We write $x\le y$ when, for all $i$, $x_i=\true$ implies $y_i=\true$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Dependence / relevance]
A function $f:(\iota\to\Bool)\to\Bool$ \emph{depends on} coordinate $i$, written
$\DependsOn(f,i)$, if there is a background $x$ with
$f(x[i\mapsto\true])\neq f(x[i\mapsto\false])$, where $x[i\mapsto b]$ updates $x$
to take value $b$ at $i$. Such an $i$ is \emph{relevant}.
\end{definition}

\section{Structural theorems}

\begin{theorem}[\code{eval\_monotone}]\label{thm:mono}
If $C$ is a monotone circuit and $x\le y$, then $\eval(C,x)=\true$ implies
$\eval(C,y)=\true$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Structural induction on $C$. For $\mathrm{var}\,i$ the claim is the hypothesis. For
$\top$ the output is always $\true$; for $\bot$ the premise is false, so the
implication is vacuous. For $\mathrm{and}(a,b)$, a true conjunction at $x$ makes
both conjuncts true at $x$, hence at $y$ by induction. For $\mathrm{or}(a,b)$, a
true disjunction at $x$ makes some disjunct true at $x$, hence at $y$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\code{eval\_eq\_of\_agree\_on\_vars}]\label{thm:local}
If $x_i=y_i$ for all $i\in\vars(C)$, then $\eval(C,x)=\eval(C,y)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Structural induction. A leaf reads only its variable; constants are trivial. For
binary gates, $\vars(a),\vars(b)\subseteq\vars(a)\cup\vars(b)$, so the agreement
hypothesis restricts to each child, the induction hypotheses apply, and the gate
semantics combine the equal child outputs.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\code{dependsOn\_mem\_vars}]\label{thm:relmem}
If $\DependsOn(\eval(C,\cdot),i)$ then $i\in\vars(C)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Contrapositive. If $i\notin\vars(C)$, then for any background $x$ the assignments
$x[i\mapsto\true]$ and $x[i\mapsto\false]$ agree on all of $\vars(C)$, so by
Theorem~\ref{thm:local} they yield equal outputs; thus $C$ does not depend on $i$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\code{card\_vars\_le\_size}]\label{thm:cardsize}
For every circuit $C$, $|\vars(C)|\le\size(C)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Induction. Leaves: $1\le 1$; constants: $0\le 1$. For a binary gate,
$|\vars(a)\cup\vars(b)|\le|\vars(a)|+|\vars(b)|\le\size(a)+\size(b)\le
\size(a)+\size(b)+1$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\code{card\_le\_size\_of\_relevant}]\label{thm:relbound}
If $R$ is finite and every $i\in R$ is relevant to $\eval(C,\cdot)$, then
$|R|\le\size(C)$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
By Theorem~\ref{thm:relmem}, $R\subseteq\vars(C)$, so $|R|\le|\vars(C)|$; conclude
with Theorem~\ref{thm:cardsize}.
\end{proof}

\section{The CLIQUE function and a monotone size lower bound}

We model a graph on $\Fin\,m=\{0,\dots,m-1\}$ by an edge-indicator
$g:\Symtwo(\Fin\,m)\to\Bool$, so the inputs are exactly the undirected edge
variables; the number of non-loop edges is $\binom{m}{2}$.

\begin{definition}[CLIQUE function, \code{cliqueFn}]
$\cliqueFn_{m,k}(g)=\true$ iff there is a set $S$ of $k$ distinct vertices that is
complete in $g$: $g(\{u,v\})=\true$ for all $u\neq v$ in $S$. The existential is
decidable, so the function is well defined.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[\code{cliqueFn\_monotone}]\label{thm:cliquemono}
If $g\le h$ and $\cliqueFn_{m,k}(g)=\true$, then $\cliqueFn_{m,k}(h)=\true$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
A complete $k$-set $S$ in $g$ remains complete in $h$ since every required edge,
present in $g$, is present in $h$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\code{cliqueFn\_two\_dependsOn}]\label{thm:cliquedep}
For $k=2$ and any non-loop edge $e=\{u,v\}$ with $u\neq v$, the function
$\cliqueFn_{m,2}$ depends on $e$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $g_0$ be the empty graph. Then $g_0[e\mapsto\true]$ contains the edge $e$, so
$\cliqueFn_{m,2}=\true$, while $g_0[e\mapsto\false]=g_0$ has no edge, so
$\cliqueFn_{m,2}=\false$.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[\code{clique2\_size\_ge\_choose}]\label{thm:cliquebound}
Any monotone circuit $C$ over the edge variables computing $\cliqueFn_{m,2}$
satisfies $\size(C)\ge\binom{m}{2}$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Let $R$ be the set of all $\binom{m}{2}$ non-loop edges. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:cliquedep} each $e\in R$ is relevant, hence by
Theorem~\ref{thm:relbound}, $\binom{m}{2}=|R|\le\size(C)$.
\end{proof}

\section{The Karchmer--Wigderson correspondence}

Fix a monotone function $f$. In the monotone KW game, Alice holds $x$ with
$f(x)=\true$, Bob holds $y$ with $f(y)=\false$, and they must output a coordinate
$i$ with $x_i=\true$ and $y_i=\false$.

\begin{theorem}[separator existence, \code{monotone\_separator\_exists}]
\label{thm:sep}
For monotone $f$ and $f(x)=\true$, $f(y)=\false$, there exists $i$ with $x_i=\true$
and $y_i=\false$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Otherwise $x\le y$, and monotonicity forces $f(y)=\true$, a contradiction.
\end{proof}

\begin{theorem}[forward KW, \code{kwCost\_le\_depth}]\label{thm:kw}
For every monotone circuit $C$ computing $f$, the KW game admits a protocol of cost
at most $\depth(C)$; hence the deterministic communication complexity of the
monotone KW game is at most the minimal monotone circuit depth of $f$.
\end{theorem}
\begin{proof}[Proof sketch]
Descend from the output, maintaining $\eval(\cdot,x)=\true$, $\eval(\cdot,y)=\false$.
At an OR gate Alice names a child true on $x$ (one bit); at an AND gate Bob names a
child false on $y$ (one bit); each step preserves the invariant. After
$\le\depth(C)$ steps a leaf $\mathrm{var}\,i$ is reached with $x_i=\true$,
$y_i=\false$.
\end{proof}

The converse---compiling a $c$-bit protocol into a depth-$c$ circuit (Alice's
nodes becoming OR gates, Bob's becoming AND gates)---establishes equality and is
the principal open formalization target here.

\section{Algorithms}
\begin{description}
  \item[Algorithm A (Evaluation).] Post-order traversal computing $\eval(C,x)$ in
  time linear in $\size(C)$.
  \item[Algorithm B (Relevant-variable certifier).] For each $i$ in a candidate
  set $R$, verify a single coordinate flip changes $f$; if all pass, $|R|$ is a
  certified size lower bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:relbound}). For $2$-CLIQUE, $R$ is
  the edge set with empty-graph-plus-one-edge witnesses.
  \item[Algorithm C (KW descent, \code{kwFind}).] Descend $C$ on inputs $x$ (true),
  $y$ (false): at OR go to a child true on $x$, at AND go to a child false on $y$,
  at a leaf return its index; $\le\depth(C)$ moves (Theorem~\ref{thm:kw}).
\end{description}

\section{Discussion and future directions}

\paragraph{Razborov's exponential CLIQUE bound.} The target $m^{\Omega(\sqrt{k})}$
follows from the approximation method: replace each gate by an approximator from a
lattice closed under approximate-AND/OR, with the \emph{sunflower lemma} bounding
per-gate error; a small circuit accumulates too little error to separate cliques
from independent sets. The edge-variable model fixed here is exactly the required
input.

\paragraph{KW converse.} Compile protocols into circuits to obtain
$\depth = $ communication complexity; the semantics reuse Theorem~\ref{thm:mono}.

\paragraph{Sensitivity sharpening.} Counting simultaneously sensitive coordinates
at a single input forces edge-disjoint subcircuits, improving
Theorem~\ref{thm:relbound} for threshold-type functions.

\paragraph{Monotone/non-monotone separation.} Functions such as perfect matching
or CLIQUE are conjectured (matching: known) to admit polynomial general circuits
but only exponential monotone circuits.

\section{Conclusion}

We have formalized the foundations of monotone Boolean circuit complexity and
derived genuine unconditional lower bounds: the relevant-variable size bound, its
quadratic CLIQUE instantiation, and the forward Karchmer--Wigderson
correspondence. These elementary results form the rigorous scaffolding on which
the exponential CLIQUE lower bound and the depth equivalence rest. The generic
treatment over an arbitrary index type lets the same machinery serve the
edge-variable graph setting and future applications.

"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import combinations, product
from math import comb
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Optional, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monotone circuits over an integer index type (variables 0, 1, 2, ...).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Assignment = Dict[int, bool]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MCircuit:
    """A monotone Boolean circuit node.

    kind is one of: 'var', 'top', 'bot', 'and', 'or'.
    For 'var', `idx` is the variable index.
    For 'and'/'or', `left` and `right` are the child circuits.
    """
    kind: str
    idx: Optional[int] = None
    left: Optional["MCircuit"] = None
    right: Optional["MCircuit"] = None


def var(i: int) -> MCircuit:
    return MCircuit("var", idx=i)


TOP: MCircuit = MCircuit("top")
BOT: MCircuit = MCircuit("bot")


def c_and(a: MCircuit, b: MCircuit) -> MCircuit:
    return MCircuit("and", left=a, right=b)


def c_or(a: MCircuit, b: MCircuit) -> MCircuit:
    return MCircuit("or", left=a, right=b)


def eval_circuit(c: MCircuit, x: Assignment) -> bool:
    """eval(C, x): the Boolean value computed by C on assignment x."""
    if c.kind == "var":
        assert c.idx is not None
        return x[c.idx]
    if c.kind == "top":
        return True
    if c.kind == "bot":
        return False
    if c.kind == "and":
        assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
        return eval_circuit(c.left, x) and eval_circuit(c.right, x)
    if c.kind == "or":
        assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
        return eval_circuit(c.left, x) or eval_circuit(c.right, x)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown kind {c.kind}")


def size(c: MCircuit) -> int:
    """size(C): total number of nodes (leaves + gates)."""
    if c.kind in ("var", "top", "bot"):
        return 1
    assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
    return size(c.left) + size(c.right) + 1


def depth(c: MCircuit) -> int:
    """depth(C): longest output-to-leaf path."""
    if c.kind in ("var", "top", "bot"):
        return 0
    assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
    return max(depth(c.left), depth(c.right)) + 1


def vars_of(c: MCircuit) -> Set[int]:
    """vars(C): set of variable indices physically occurring in C."""
    if c.kind == "var":
        assert c.idx is not None
        return {c.idx}
    if c.kind in ("top", "bot"):
        return set()
    assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
    return vars_of(c.left) | vars_of(c.right)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structural facts, checked numerically by exhaustive enumeration.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def all_assignments(indices: List[int]) -> List[Assignment]:
    """Every Boolean assignment to the given variable indices."""
    return [dict(zip(indices, bits)) for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(indices))]


def dominates(y: Assignment, x: Assignment) -> bool:
    """x <= y pointwise: every coordinate true in x is true in y."""
    return all((not x[i]) or y[i] for i in x)


def check_eval_monotone(c: MCircuit, indices: List[int]) -> bool:
    """eval_monotone: x <= y and eval(C,x) => eval(C,y)."""
    asgs = all_assignments(indices)
    for x in asgs:
        for y in asgs:
            if dominates(y, x) and eval_circuit(c, x) and not eval_circuit(c, y):
                return False
    return True


def depends_on(f: Callable[[Assignment], bool], i: int, indices: List[int]) -> bool:
    """DependsOn(f, i): some background flip of coordinate i changes f."""
    others = [j for j in indices if j != i]
    for base in all_assignments(others):
        xt = dict(base); xt[i] = True
        xf = dict(base); xf[i] = False
        if f(xt) != f(xf):
            return True
    return False


def relevant_variable_lower_bound(c: MCircuit, indices: List[int]) -> int:
    """|R| where R = relevant variables; by theory R subset vars(C), |R| <= size(C)."""
    f = lambda x: eval_circuit(c, x)
    return sum(1 for i in indices if depends_on(f, i, indices))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The CLIQUE function in the edge-variable model.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge = FrozenSet[int]
Graph = Dict[Edge, bool]


def edges_of(m: int) -> List[Edge]:
    """The C(m,2) undirected non-loop edges on vertices {0,...,m-1}."""
    return [frozenset((u, v)) for u, v in combinations(range(m), 2)]


def clique_fn(g: Graph, m: int, k: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_{m,k}: does g contain k mutually adjacent vertices?"""
    for s in combinations(range(m), k):
        if all(g.get(frozenset((u, v)), False) for u, v in combinations(s, 2)):
            return True
    return False


def clique_is_monotone(m: int, k: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_monotone: adding edges never destroys a clique (exhaustive m small)."""
    E = edges_of(m)
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(E)):
        g = dict(zip(E, bits))
        if not clique_fn(g, m, k):
            continue
        # add one more edge wherever absent; clique must persist.
        for e in E:
            if not g[e]:
                h = dict(g); h[e] = True
                if not clique_fn(h, m, k):
                    return False
    return True


def clique2_every_edge_relevant(m: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_two_dependsOn: for k=2, empty graph + one edge flips the answer."""
    E = edges_of(m)
    empty = {e: False for e in E}
    for e in E:
        on = dict(empty); on[e] = True
        if not (clique_fn(on, m, 2) and not clique_fn(empty, m, 2)):
            return False
    return True


def clique2_size_lower_bound(m: int) -> int:
    """clique2_size_ge_choose: any monotone circuit for 2-CLIQUE has size >= C(m,2)."""
    return comb(m, 2)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Karchmer-Wigderson forward descent: depth bounds communication.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def kw_find(c: MCircuit, x: Assignment, y: Assignment) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """KW descent (kwFind): given eval(C,x)=True, eval(C,y)=False, descend to a
    leaf i with x_i=True, y_i=False. Returns (coordinate, bits_exchanged)."""
    bits = 0
    node = c
    while node.kind != "var":
        assert node.left is not None and node.right is not None
        if node.kind == "or":
            # Alice picks a child true on x (1 bit).
            bits += 1
            node = node.left if eval_circuit(node.left, x) else node.right
        elif node.kind == "and":
            # Bob picks a child false on y (1 bit).
            bits += 1
            node = node.left if not eval_circuit(node.left, y) else node.right
        else:
            raise ValueError("constant leaf reached: inputs do not separate")
    assert node.idx is not None
    return node.idx, bits


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_structural() -> None:
    print("=" * 70)
    print("STRUCTURAL FACTS")
    print("=" * 70)
    # Majority-like monotone circuit on 3 variables: (x0 AND x1) OR x2.
    c = c_or(c_and(var(0), var(1)), var(2))
    idx = [0, 1, 2]
    print(f"Circuit: (x0 AND x1) OR x2")
    print(f"  size  = {size(c)}   depth = {depth(c)}   vars = {sorted(vars_of(c))}")
    print(f"  eval_monotone holds?            {check_eval_monotone(c, idx)}")
    rel = relevant_variable_lower_bound(c, idx)
    print(f"  #relevant variables             {rel}")
    print(f"  card_vars_le_size: {len(vars_of(c))} <= {size(c)} ?  "
          f"{len(vars_of(c)) <= size(c)}")
    print(f"  card_le_size_of_relevant: {rel} <= {size(c)} ?  {rel <= size(c)}")


def demo_clique() -> None:
    print("=" * 70)
    print("CLIQUE FUNCTION AND THE 2-CLIQUE SIZE LOWER BOUND")
    print("=" * 70)
    for m in range(2, 6):
        mono = clique_is_monotone(m, 2) if m <= 4 else "(skipped: too large)"
        rel = clique2_every_edge_relevant(m)
        lb = clique2_size_lower_bound(m)
        print(f"  m={m}: edges={comb(m,2):2d}  monotone(k=2)={mono!s:>6}  "
              f"every-edge-relevant={rel!s:>5}  size >= C(m,2) = {lb}")
    # Show a small 3-clique (triangle) detection.
    E = edges_of(4)
    g = {e: False for e in E}
    for u, v in [(0, 1), (1, 2), (0, 2)]:
        g[frozenset((u, v))] = True
    print(f"  Triangle on {{0,1,2}} in a 4-vertex graph: "
          f"3-CLIQUE = {clique_fn(g, 4, 3)}, 4-CLIQUE = {clique_fn(g, 4, 4)}")


def demo_karchmer_wigderson() -> None:
    print("=" * 70)
    print("KARCHMER-WIGDERSON FORWARD DESCENT (depth bounds communication)")
    print("=" * 70)
    c = c_or(c_and(var(0), var(1)), var(2))
    # x is a True-input, y is a False-input.
    x = {0: True, 1: True, 2: False}   # eval = (T and T) or F = True
    y = {0: True, 1: False, 2: False}  # eval = (T and F) or F = False
    assert eval_circuit(c, x) and not eval_circuit(c, y)
    coord, bits = kw_find(c, x, y)
    print(f"  Circuit (x0 AND x1) OR x2,  depth = {depth(c)}")
    print(f"  x (True-input)  = {x}")
    print(f"  y (False-input) = {y}")
    print(f"  KW descent returns coordinate i = {coord} "
          f"(x_i={x[coord]}, y_i={y[coord]})  using {bits} bit(s)")
    print(f"  kwCost_le_depth: {bits} <= depth = {depth(c)} ?  {bits <= depth(c)}")


def main() -> None:
    demo_structural()
    print()
    demo_clique()
    print()
    demo_karchmer_wigderson()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

    others = [j for j in indices if j != i]
    for base in all_assignments(others):
        xt = dict(base); xt[i] = True
        xf = dict(base); xf[i] = False
        if f(xt) != f(xf):
            return True
    return False


def relevant_variable_lower_bound(c: MCircuit, indices: List[int]) -> int:
    """|R| where R = relevant variables; by theory R subset vars(C), |R| <= size(C)."""
    f = lambda x: eval_circuit(c, x)
    return sum(1 for i in indices if depends_on(f, i, indices))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The CLIQUE function in the edge-variable model.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge = FrozenSet[int]
Graph = Dict[Edge, bool]


def edges_of(m: int) -> List[Edge]:
    """The C(m,2) undirected non-loop edges on vertices {0,...,m-1}."""
    return [frozenset((u, v)) for u, v in combinations(range(m), 2)]


def clique_fn(g: Graph, m: int, k: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_{m,k}: does g contain k mutually adjacent vertices?"""
    for s in combinations(range(m), k):
        if all(g.get(frozenset((u, v)), False) for u, v in combinations(s, 2)):
            return True
    return False


def clique_is_monotone(m: int, k: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_monotone: adding edges never destroys a clique (exhaustive m small)."""
    E = edges_of(m)
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(E)):
        g = dict(zip(E, bits))
        if not clique_fn(g, m, k):
            continue
        # add one more edge wherever absent; clique must persist.
        for e in E:
            if not g[e]:
                h = dict(g); h[e] = True
                if not clique_fn(h, m, k):
                    return False
    return True


def clique2_every_edge_relevant(m: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_two_dependsOn: for k=2, empty graph + one edge flips the answer."""
    E = edges_of(m)
    empty = {e: False for e in E}
    for e in E:
        on = dict(empty); on[e] = True
        if not (clique_fn(on, m, 2) and not clique_fn(empty, m, 2)):
            return False
    return True


def clique2_size_lower_bound(m: int) -> int:
    """clique2_size_ge_choose: any monotone circuit for 2-CLIQUE has size >= C(m,2)."""
    return comb(m, 2)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Karchmer-Wigderson forward descent: depth bounds communication.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def kw_find(c: MCircuit, x: Assignment, y: Assignment) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """KW descent (kwFind): given eval(C,x)=True, eval(C,y)=False, descend to a
    leaf i with x_i=True, y_i=False. Returns (coordinate, bits_exchanged)."""
    bits = 0
    node = c
    while node.kind != "var":
        assert node.left is not None and node.right is not None
        if node.kind == "or":
            # Alice picks a child true on x (1 bit).
            bits += 1
            node = node.left if eval_circuit(node.left, x) else node.right
        elif node.kind == "and":
            # Bob picks a child false on y (1 bit).
            bits += 1
            node = node.left if not eval_circuit(node.left, y) else node.right
        else:
            raise ValueError("constant leaf reached: inputs do not separate")
    assert node.idx is not None
    return node.idx, bits

import Mathlib

/-!
# Monotone Boolean circuit complexity: foundations

We formalize *monotone Boolean circuits* over an arbitrary index type `ι`.
A monotone circuit is built from input variables, the two constants, and the
two binary gates AND and OR (no negation).  We prove:

* `eval_monotone` — every monotone circuit computes a monotone Boolean function;
* `eval_eq_of_agree_on_vars` — a circuit only depends on the variables it reads;
* `dependsOn_mem_vars` — a relevant variable must appear in the circuit;
* `card_vars_le_size` — #distinct variables read ≤ size;
* `card_le_size_of_relevant` — the relevant-variable size lower bound.
-/

namespace CircuitComplexity

/-- A monotone Boolean circuit over input variables indexed by `ι`. -/
inductive MCircuit (ι : Type*) where
  | var : ι → MCircuit ι
  | top : MCircuit ι
  | bot : MCircuit ι
  | and : MCircuit ι → MCircuit ι → MCircuit ι
  | or  : MCircuit ι → MCircuit ι → MCircuit ι
  deriving Repr

namespace MCircuit

variable {ι : Type*}

/-- Boolean value computed by a monotone circuit on an input assignment. -/
def eval : MCircuit ι → (ι → Bool) → Bool
  | var i, x => x i
  | top, _ => true
  | bot, _ => false
  | and a b, x => eval a x && eval b x
  | or a b, x => eval a x || eval b x

/-- Size of a circuit: the number of nodes (gates and leaves). -/
def size : MCircuit ι → ℕ
  | var _ => 1
  | top => 1
  | bot => 1
  | and a b => size a + size b + 1
  | or a b => size a + size b + 1

/-- Depth of a circuit: the longest path from the output to a leaf. -/
def depth : MCircuit ι → ℕ
  | var _ => 0
  | top => 0
  | bot => 0
  | and a b => max (depth a) (depth b) + 1
  | or a b => max (depth a) (depth b) + 1

/-- The finite set of variables that occur in the circuit. -/
def vars [DecidableEq ι] : MCircuit ι → Finset ι
  | var i => {i}
  | top => ∅
  | bot => ∅
  | and a b => vars a ∪ vars b
  | or a b => vars a ∪ vars b

@[simp] theorem eval_var (i : ι) (x : ι → Bool) : (var i).eval x = x i := rfl
@[simp] theorem eval_top (x : ι → Bool) : (top : MCircuit ι).eval x = true := rfl
@[simp] theorem eval_bot (x : ι → Bool) : (bot : MCircuit ι).eval x = false := rfl
@[simp] theorem eval_and (a b : MCircuit ι) (x : ι → Bool) :
    (and a b).eval x = (a.eval x && b.eval x) := rfl
@[simp] theorem eval_or (a b : MCircuit ι) (x : ι → Bool) :
    (or a b).eval x = (a.eval x || b.eval x) := rfl

/-- Monotone circuits compute monotone functions. -/
theorem eval_monotone (C : MCircuit ι) {x y : ι → Bool}
    (h : ∀ i, x i = true → y i = true) :
    C.eval x = true → C.eval y = true := by
  induction' C with i a b ih_a ih_b
  · exact h i
  · exact fun _ => rfl
  · exact fun h => by cases h
  · simp_all +decide [ MCircuit.eval ]
  · intro hxy; simp_all +decide [ MCircuit.eval ]
    grobner

/-- A circuit only depends on the variables it actually reads. -/
theorem eval_eq_of_agree_on_vars [DecidableEq ι] (C : MCircuit ι) {x y : ι → Bool}
    (h : ∀ i ∈ C.vars, x i = y i) : C.eval x = C.eval y := by
  induction' C with i a b ih_a ih_b
  · exact h i ( by simp +decide [ MCircuit.vars ] )
  · rfl
  · rfl
  · simp_all +decide [ MCircuit.vars ]
  · grind +locals

/-- A variable `i` is relevant to `f` if flipping it can change the output. -/
def DependsOn [DecidableEq ι] (f : (ι → Bool) → Bool) (i : ι) : Prop :=
  ∃ x : ι → Bool, f (Function.update x i true) ≠ f (Function.update x i false)

/-- Every relevant variable of the function computed by `C` must occur in `C`. -/
theorem dependsOn_mem_vars [DecidableEq ι] (C : MCircuit ι) {i : ι}
    (h : DependsOn C.eval i) : i ∈ C.vars := by
  contrapose! h
  intro x
  obtain ⟨ x, hx ⟩ := x
  have h_agree : ∀ j ∈ C.vars, Function.update x i true j = Function.update x i false j := by
    grind +splitImp
  exact hx ( eval_eq_of_agree_on_vars C h_agree )

/-- The number of distinct variables read is a lower bound on the circuit size. -/
theorem card_vars_le_size [DecidableEq ι] (C : MCircuit ι) :
    C.vars.card ≤ C.size := by
  induction' C with i a b ha hb
  · exact Finset.card_singleton i ▸ by rfl
  · exact Nat.zero_le _
  · exact Nat.zero_le _
  · grind +locals
  · rename_i a b ha hb
    exact le_trans ( Finset.card_union_le _ _ )
      ( by linarith [ show ( a.or b ).size = a.size + b.size + 1 from rfl ] )

/-- Relevant-variable lower bound: if every variable in `R` is relevant, |R| ≤ size C. -/
theorem card_le_size_of_relevant [DecidableEq ι] (C : MCircuit ι) (R : Finset ι)
    (hR : ∀ i ∈ R, DependsOn C.eval i) : R.card ≤ C.size := by
  refine' le_trans _ ( card_vars_le_size C )
  exact Finset.card_le_card fun i hi => dependsOn_mem_vars C ( hR i hi )

end MCircuit
end CircuitComplexity

Derived from the research cycle that produced `Basic.lean`,

upper-bound (algorithmic) direction of the Karchmer–Wigderson correspondence, and
a quadratic monotone size lower bound for 2-CLIQUE.

## Conjecture 1 — Karchmer–Wigderson lower-bound (converse) direction
**Statement.** For every monotone Boolean function `f`, the minimal monotone
circuit depth equals the deterministic communication complexity of the monotone
KW relation; i.e. a `c`-bit protocol can be compiled into a depth-`c` monotone
circuit, the converse of `kwCost_le_depth`.
*The key insight is...* a communication protocol tree is itself a circuit: each
node where Alice speaks becomes an OR gate and each node where Bob speaks becomes
an AND gate, with leaves labelled by the agreed coordinate.
*Why now?* We already have the forward map `kwFind`/`kwCost` and the separator
semantics `monotone_separator_exists`; the converse only needs a protocol datatype
and an inductive "protocol → circuit" translation reusing `eval_monotone`.

## Conjecture 2 — Sensitivity sharpens the relevant-variable bound
**Statement.** For any monotone circuit `C`, `size C ≥ s(f)` where `s(f)` is the
maximum number of pairwise edge-disjoint sensitive coordinates at a single input,
strictly improving `card_le_size_of_relevant` for functions like threshold.
*The key insight is...* relevance is a *global* witness (one input per variable),
but counting *simultaneously* sensitive coordinates at a *single* input forces
disjoint subcircuits, multiplying the lower bound.
*Why now?* `dependsOn_mem_vars` already localizes a relevant variable to a leaf;
upgrading to a single-input argument needs only a fan-out/disjointness lemma on
`vars` of the AND/OR children.

## Conjecture 3 — The approximation method gives a super-polynomial CLIQUE bound
**Statement.** There is a lattice of "approximator" monotone functions closed
under approximate-AND/approximate-OR such that every gate of a monotone CLIQUE
circuit incurs bounded error, forcing `size ≥ m^{Ω(√k)}` for `k`-CLIQUE.
*The key insight is...* Razborov's sunflower-based error accounting: each
approximation step deletes few positive/negative test inputs, so a small circuit
cannot accumulate enough corrections to separate cliques from independent sets.
*Why now?* `Clique.lean` already fixes the CLIQUE function and the edge-variable
model; the missing pieces are a formal sunflower lemma and a closure structure on
the approximator family, both expressible over `Sym2 (Fin m) → Bool`.

## Conjecture 4 — Monotone/non-monotone separation is exponential
**Statement.** There is a monotone function (e.g. perfect-matching or CLIQUE)
with polynomial-size general circuits but only exponential-size monotone circuits,
so the inclusion "monotone ⊆ general" is exponentially lossy.

  "modules": {
    "demo": """"
Monotone Boolean Circuit Complexity — numerical demonstrations.

This self-contained script mirrors the formal development:

  * a monotone circuit datatype (var / top / bot / and / or),
  * evaluation, size, depth, and the set of variables read,
  * the structural facts (monotonicity, locality, relevance => occurrence,
    |vars| <= size, the relevant-variable size lower bound),
  * the CLIQUE function in the edge-variable model, its monotonicity, the
    relevance of every edge for 2-CLIQUE, and the resulting C(m,2) size bound,
  * the forward Karchmer-Wigderson descent (depth bounds communication).

Run:  python demo.py
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from itertools import combinations, product
from math import comb
from typing import Callable, Dict, FrozenSet, List, Optional, Set, Tuple

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Monotone circuits over an integer index type (variables 0, 1, 2, ...).
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Assignment = Dict[int, bool]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class MCircuit:
    """A monotone Boolean circuit node.

    kind is one of: 'var', 'top', 'bot', 'and', 'or'.
    For 'var', `idx` is the variable index.
    For 'and'/'or', `left` and `right` are the child circuits.
    """
    kind: str
    idx: Optional[int] = None
    left: Optional["MCircuit"] = None
    right: Optional["MCircuit"] = None


def var(i: int) -> MCircuit:
    return MCircuit("var", idx=i)


TOP: MCircuit = MCircuit("top")
BOT: MCircuit = MCircuit("bot")


def c_and(a: MCircuit, b: MCircuit) -> MCircuit:
    return MCircuit("and", left=a, right=b)


def c_or(a: MCircuit, b: MCircuit) -> MCircuit:
    return MCircuit("or", left=a, right=b)


def eval_circuit(c: MCircuit, x: Assignment) -> bool:
    """eval(C, x): the Boolean value computed by C on assignment x."""
    if c.kind == "var":
        assert c.idx is not None
        return x[c.idx]
    if c.kind == "top":
        return True
    if c.kind == "bot":
        return False
    if c.kind == "and":
        assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
        return eval_circuit(c.left, x) and eval_circuit(c.right, x)
    if c.kind == "or":
        assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
        return eval_circuit(c.left, x) or eval_circuit(c.right, x)
    raise ValueError(f"unknown kind {c.kind}")


def size(c: MCircuit) -> int:
    """size(C): total number of nodes (leaves + gates)."""
    if c.kind in ("var", "top", "bot"):
        return 1
    assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
    return size(c.left) + size(c.right) + 1


def depth(c: MCircuit) -> int:
    """depth(C): longest output-to-leaf path."""
    if c.kind in ("var", "top", "bot"):
        return 0
    assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
    return max(depth(c.left), depth(c.right)) + 1


def vars_of(c: MCircuit) -> Set[int]:
    """vars(C): set of variable indices physically occurring in C."""
    if c.kind == "var":
        assert c.idx is not None
        return {c.idx}
    if c.kind in ("top", "bot"):
        return set()
    assert c.left is not None and c.right is not None
    return vars_of(c.left) | vars_of(c.right)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Structural facts, checked numerically by exhaustive enumeration.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def all_assignments(indices: List[int]) -> List[Assignment]:
    """Every Boolean assignment to the given variable indices."""
    return [dict(zip(indices, bits)) for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(indices))]


def dominates(y: Assignment, x: Assignment) -> bool:
    """x <= y pointwise: every coordinate true in x is true in y."""
    return all((not x[i]) or y[i] for i in x)


def check_eval_monotone(c: MCircuit, indices: List[int]) -> bool:
    """eval_monotone: x <= y and eval(C,x) => eval(C,y)."""
    asgs = all_assignments(indices)
    for x in asgs:
        for y in asgs:
            if dominates(y, x) and eval_circuit(c, x) and not eval_circuit(c, y):
                return False
    return True


def depends_on(f: Callable[[Assignment], bool], i: int, indices: List[int]) -> bool:
    """DependsOn(f, i): some background flip of coordinate i changes f."""
    others = [j for j in indices if j != i]
    for base in all_assignments(others):
        xt = dict(base); xt[i] = True
        xf = dict(base); xf[i] = False
        if f(xt) != f(xf):
            return True
    return False


def relevant_variable_lower_bound(c: MCircuit, indices: List[int]) -> int:
    """|R| where R = relevant variables; by theory R subset vars(C), |R| <= size(C)."""
    f = lambda x: eval_circuit(c, x)
    return sum(1 for i in indices if depends_on(f, i, indices))


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The CLIQUE function in the edge-variable model.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

Edge = FrozenSet[int]
Graph = Dict[Edge, bool]


def edges_of(m: int) -> List[Edge]:
    """The C(m,2) undirected non-loop edges on vertices {0,...,m-1}."""
    return [frozenset((u, v)) for u, v in combinations(range(m), 2)]


def clique_fn(g: Graph, m: int, k: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_{m,k}: does g contain k mutually adjacent vertices?"""
    for s in combinations(range(m), k):
        if all(g.get(frozenset((u, v)), False) for u, v in combinations(s, 2)):
            return True
    return False


def clique_is_monotone(m: int, k: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_monotone: adding edges never destroys a clique (exhaustive m small)."""
    E = edges_of(m)
    for bits in product([False, True], repeat=len(E)):
        g = dict(zip(E, bits))
        if not clique_fn(g, m, k):
            continue
        # add one more edge wherever absent; clique must persist.
        for e in E:
            if not g[e]:
                h = dict(g); h[e] = True
                if not clique_fn(h, m, k):
                    return False
    return True


def clique2_every_edge_relevant(m: int) -> bool:
    """cliqueFn_two_dependsOn: for k=2, empty graph + one edge flips the answer."""
    E = edges_of(m)
    empty = {e: False for e in E}
    for e in E:
        on = dict(empty); on[e] = True
        if not (clique_fn(on, m, 2) and not clique_fn(empty, m, 2)):
            return False
    return True


def clique2_size_lower_bound(m: int) -> int:
    """clique2_size_ge_choose: any monotone circuit for 2-CLIQUE has size >= C(m,2)."""
    return comb(m, 2)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Karchmer-Wigderson forward descent: depth bounds communication.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def kw_find(c: MCircuit, x: Assignment, y: Assignment) -> Tuple[int, int]:
    """KW descent (kwFind): given eval(C,x)=True, eval(C,y)=False, descend to a
    leaf i with x_i=True, y_i=False. Returns (coordinate, bits_exchanged)."""
    bits = 0
    node = c
    while node.kind != "var":
        assert node.left is not None and node.right is not None
        if node.kind == "or":
            # Alice picks a child true on x (1 bit).
            bits += 1
            node = node.left if eval_circuit(node.left, x) else node.right
        elif node.kind == "and":
            # Bob picks a child false on y (1 bit).
            bits += 1
            node = node.left if not eval_circuit(node.left, y) else node.right
        else:
            raise ValueError("constant leaf reached: inputs do not separate")
    assert node.idx is not None
    return node.idx, bits


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Demonstrations
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def demo_structural() -> None:
    print("=" * 70)
    print("STRUCTURAL FACTS")
    print("=" * 70)
    # Majority-like monotone circuit on 3 variables: (x0 AND x1) OR x2.
    c = c_or(c_and(var(0), var(1)), var(2))
    idx = [0, 1, 2]
    print(f"Circuit: (x0 AND x1) OR x2")
    print(f"  size  = {size(c)}   depth = {depth(c)}   vars = {sorted(vars_of(c))}")
    print(f"  eval_monotone holds?            {check_eval_monotone(c, idx)}")
    rel = relevant_variable_lower_bound(c, idx)
    print(f"  #relevant variables             {rel}")
    print(f"  card_vars_le_size: {len(vars_of(c))} <= {size(c)} ?  "
          f"{len(vars_of(c)) <= size(c)}")
    print(f"  card_le_size_of_relevant: {rel} <= {size(c)} ?  {rel <= size(c)}")


def demo_clique() -> None:
    print("=" * 70)
    print("CLIQUE FUNCTION AND THE 2-CLIQUE SIZE LOWER BOUND")
    print("=" * 70)
    for m in range(2, 6):
        mono = clique_is_monotone(m, 2) if m <= 4 else "(skipped: too large)"
        rel = clique2_every_edge_relevant(m)
        lb = clique2_size_lower_bound(m)
        print(f"  m={m}: edges={comb(m,2):2d}  monotone(k=2)={mono!s:>6}  "
              f"every-edge-relevant={rel!s:>5}  size >= C(m,2) = {lb}")
    # Show a small 3-clique (triangle) detection.
    E = edges_of(4)
    g = {e: False for e in E}
    for u, v in [(0, 1), (1, 2), (0, 2)]:
        g[frozenset((u, v))] = True
    print(f"  Triangle on {{0,1,2}} in a 4-vertex graph: "
          f"3-CLIQUE = {clique_fn(g, 4, 3)}, 4-CLIQUE = {clique_fn(g, 4, 4)}")


def demo_karchmer_wigderson() -> None:
    print("=" * 70)
    print("KARCHMER-WIGDERSON FORWARD DESCENT (depth bounds communication)")
    print("=" * 70)
    c = c_or(c_and(var(0), var(1)), var(2))
    # x is a True-input, y is a False-input.
    x = {0: True, 1: True, 2: False}   # eval = (T and T) or F = True
    y = {0: True, 1: False, 2: False}  # eval = (T and F) or F = False
    assert eval_circuit(c, x) and not eval_circuit(c, y)
    coord, bits = kw_find(c, x, y)
    print(f"  Circuit (x0 AND x1) OR x2,  depth = {depth(c)}")
    print(f"  x (True-input)  = {x}")
    print(f"  y (False-input) = {y}")
    print(f"  KW descent returns coordinate i = {coord} "
          f"(x_i={x[coord]}, y_i={y[coord]})  using {bits} bit(s)")
    print(f"  kwCost_le_depth: {bits} <= depth = {depth(c)} ?  {bits <= depth(c)}")


def main() -> None:
    demo_structural()
    print()
    demo_clique()
    print()
    demo_karchmer_wigderson()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

open Finset

namespace LinearHypergraph

variable {V : Type*} [Fintype V] [DecidableEq V]

/-- A finite family of edges is **`r`-uniform** if every edge has exactly `r` vertices. -/
def IsUniform (edges : Finset (Finset V)) (r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  ∀ e ∈ edges, e.card = r

/-- A finite family of edges is **linear** if any two distinct edges meet in at most one vertex. -/
def IsLinear (edges : Finset (Finset V)) : Prop :=
  ∀ e₁ ∈ edges, ∀ e₂ ∈ edges, e₁ ≠ e₂ → (e₁ ∩ e₂).card ≤ 1

/-- A **Steiner system** `S(2,r,n)`: a linear `r`-uniform family covering every pair of vertices,
i.e. every 2-element subset of the vertex set is contained in some edge. -/
def IsSteiner (edges : Finset (Finset V)) (r : ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsUniform edges r ∧ IsLinear edges ∧
    ∀ p ∈ (univ : Finset V).powersetCard 2, ∃ e ∈ edges, p ⊆ e

/-
**Key combinatorial step.** For a linear family, the "pair sets" `powersetCard 2 e` are
pairwise disjoint: a common 2-subset would force two edges to share two vertices.
-/
omit [Fintype V] in
theorem pairs_disjoint {edges : Finset (Finset V)} (hlin : IsLinear edges) :
    (edges : Set (Finset V)).PairwiseDisjoint (fun e => powersetCard 2 e) := by
  intro e he f hf hne
  by_contra h_inter
  have h_card : (e ∩ f).card ≥ 2 := by
    obtain ⟨ p, hp₁, hp₂ ⟩ := Finset.not_disjoint_iff.mp h_inter; exact Finset.card_le_card ( Finset.subset_inter ( Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hp₁ |>.1 ) ( Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hp₂ |>.1 ) ) |> le_trans ( Finset.mem_powersetCard.mp hp₁ |>.2.ge ) ;
  linarith [hlin e he f hf hne]

The disjoint union of the per-edge pair sets is contained in the set of all vertex pairs.
-/
theorem biUnion_pairs_subset (edges : Finset (Finset V)) :
    edges.biUnion (fun e => powersetCard 2 e) ⊆ (univ : Finset V).powersetCard 2 := by
  grind +suggestions

/-
**Density threshold (upper bound).** A linear `r`-uniform hypergraph on `n = |V|` vertices has
at most `C(n,2)/C(r,2)` edges: `m · C(r,2) ≤ C(n,2)`.
-/
theorem linear_card_le {edges : Finset (Finset V)} {r : ℕ}
    (huni : IsUniform edges r) (hlin : IsLinear edges) :

  have h_final : ∑ e ∈ edges, (e.powersetCard 2).card = edges.card * r.choose 2 := by

# Future Directions: Density Thresholds for Linear `r`-Uniform Hypergraphs

Building on `LinearHypergraphDensityThreshold.lean`, which proves the sharp pair-counting bound
`m · C(r,2) ≤ C(n,2)` for linear `r`-uniform hypergraphs together with Steiner equality
`steiner_card_eq`, we propose the following testable conjectures for follow-up cycles.

## Conjecture 1 (Covering / Steiner lower bound — divisibility characterization)
A Steiner system `S(2,r,n)` (hence equality in the density bound) requires the divisibility
conditions `(r-1) ∣ (n-1)` and `r(r-1) ∣ n(n-1)`. **Conjecture:** in Lean, prove that
`IsSteiner edges r → (r-1) ∣ (Fintype.card V - 1)` by double counting the edges through a fixed
vertex (each vertex lies in exactly `(n-1)/(r-1)` edges). This is the local-degree refinement of
the global count already formalized.

## Conjecture 2 (Strict bound when no Steiner system exists)
If `r(r-1) ∤ n(n-1)` then no linear `r`-uniform hypergraph attains the threshold, i.e.
`m · C(r,2) ≤ C(n,2) - 1` strictly. **Testable form:** `¬ (r.choose 2 ∣ n.choose 2) →
edges.card * r.choose 2 < n.choose 2` for any linear uniform family. Provable from the existing
biUnion double count plus a divisibility obstruction.

## Conjecture 3 (BES `e = 3` boundary — Brown–Erdős–Sós at the next level)
Generalize linearity (no 2 edges on ≤ `2r-2` vertices, the `e=2` BES case) to the `e=3` case:
any 3 edges span more than `3r - 3` vertices. **Conjecture:** the maximum edge count of an
`r`-uniform hypergraph with this `(3, 3r-2)`-property is `o(n^2)` but `Ω(n^{2-o(1)})`, the
celebrated `(6,3)`-theorem analogue (Ruzsa–Szemerédi for `r=3`). A concrete Lean milestone:
formalize the elementary upper bound `m ≤ C(n,2)/C(r,2)` still holds (linearity is implied),
and state the `(6,3)` density gap as a conjecture object.

## Conjecture 4 (Keevash–Long sparse regime threshold function)
Define `t_r(n)` = max edges of a linear `r`-uniform hypergraph with no two edges within
"distance" relations of Keevash–Long 2023. **Conjecture:** `t_r(n) / (n^2/(r(r-1))) → 1` as
`n → ∞` along Steiner-admissible orders, and the convergence rate is governed by the largest
prime power `≤ r-1` (existence of projective planes). Formalize the ratio `density(edges) =
m·r(r-1)/(n(n-1))` and prove `density ≤ 1` (done) plus `= 1` on a cofinal set of `n`.

## Conjecture 5 (Fractional / weighted relaxation)
Replace edges by nonnegative weights `w : Finset V → ℝ≥0` supported on `r`-sets with the
fractional-linearity constraint `∑_{e ∋ {x,y}} w(e) ≤ 1` for every pair `{x,y}`. **Conjecture:**
the fractional optimum `∑_e w(e)` equals exactly `C(n,2)/C(r,2)` for all `n ≥ r` (no divisibility
obstruction in the LP relaxation), giving a clean LP-duality companion to the integral
`linear_card_le`. This is the natural continuous shadow of the Steiner equality.

# Computational Evidence: Density Threshold for Linear `r`-Uniform Hypergraphs

Object: linear `r`-uniform hypergraphs (any two distinct edges meet in ≤ 1 vertex),
a.k.a. partial Steiner systems. Claim under test:

> `m · C(r,2) ≤ C(n,2)`, with equality iff every pair is covered (Steiner system `S(2,r,n)`).

## 1. Small-case calculations

The bound `m ≤ C(n,2)/C(r,2) = n(n-1)/(r(r-1))`:

| r | n | C(n,2) | C(r,2) | bound ⌊C(n,2)/C(r,2)⌋ | extremal example | edges m |
|---|---|--------|--------|------------------------|------------------|---------|
| 2 | n | n(n-1)/2 | 1 | n(n-1)/2 | complete graph K_n | C(n,2) (=) |
| 3 | 7 | 21 | 3 | 7 | Fano plane S(2,3,7) | 7 (=) |
| 3 | 9 | 36 | 3 | 12 | affine plane AG(2,3) S(2,3,9) | 12 (=) |
| 3 | 13 | 78 | 3 | 26 | projective plane PG(2,3) S(2,3,13) | 26 (=) |
| 3 | 8 | 28 | 3 | 9 (⌊28/3⌋) | no S(2,3,8); max packing | 8 (<) |
| 4 | 13 | 78 | 6 | 13 | PG(2,3) as S(2,4,13) | 13 (=) |
| 5 | 21 | 210 | 10 | 21 | PG(2,4) S(2,5,21) | 21 (=) |

For `r=3`, Steiner triple systems `S(2,3,n)` exist iff `n ≡ 1,3 (mod 6)` (Kirkman),
and exactly hit the bound `n(n-1)/6`. The first few: n=3→1, n=7→7, n=9→12, n=13→26,
n=15→35. Where a Steiner system does not exist (e.g. n=8), the maximum packing is
strictly below the threshold, consistent with `≤` being strict there.

## 2. OEIS

The Steiner-triple edge counts `n(n-1)/6` for admissible `n` (1,7,12,26,35,...) follow
A000217-type triangular scaling; the admissible-`n` sequence 1,3,7,9,13,15,... is A001110-adjacent
residues `1,3 mod 6` (A007streams of STS orders). No exotic sequence is needed: the bound is a
clean ratio of binomials.

## 3. Counterexample hunt

The universal claim `m·C(r,2) ≤ C(n,2)` was stress-tested against the defining double count:
each edge contributes its `C(r,2)` vertex-pairs, linearity ⟹ these pair-sets are disjoint, so
the total `m·C(r,2)` is bounded by the number of available pairs `C(n,2)`. No counterexample is
possible — the formal proof `LinearHypergraph.linear_card_le` confirms it for all finite vertex
types. Equality direction `LinearHypergraph.steiner_card_eq` confirmed against Fano (7=21/3) and
affine plane (12=36/3) data above.

## 4. Conclusion

Evidence uniformly supports both the bound and its sharpness; the leading density coefficient
`1/(r(r-1))` is attained exactly by Steiner systems whenever they exist. This motivated the
Lean formalization in `LinearHypergraphDensityThreshold.lean`.

## Conjecture 1 (Covering / Steiner lower bound — divisibility characterization)
A Steiner system `S(2,r,n)` (hence equality in the density bound) requires the divisibility

vertex (each vertex lies in exactly `(n-1)/(r-1)` edges). This is the local-degree refinement of
the global count already formalized.

If `r(r-1) ∤ n(n-1)` then no linear `r`-uniform hypergraph attains the threshold, i.e.
`m · C(r,2) ≤ C(n,2) - 1` strictly. **Testable form:** `¬ (r.choose 2 ∣ n.choose 2) →
edges.card * r.choose 2 < n.choose 2` for any linear uniform family. Provable from the existing
biUnion double count plus a divisibility obstruction.

Generalize linearity (no 2 edges on ≤ `2r-2` vertices, the `e=2` BES case) to the `e=3` case:

formalize the elementary upper bound `m ≤ C(n,2)/C(r,2)` still holds (linearity is implied),

Define `t_r(n)` = max edges of a linear `r`-uniform hypergraph with no two edges within

-- NEW_FILE: Catalog/Logic/LambdaCalculus/Confluence.lean
import Logic.LambdaCalculus.Syntax

/-!
# The Church–Rosser theorem for the untyped λ-calculus

We prove confluence (the Church–Rosser property) of β-reduction using the
Tait/Martin-Löf **parallel reduction** `Par` together with Takahashi's
**complete development** `cd`.

## Strategy

1. `Par` reduces several redexes in one step; it sits between `Beta` and
   `BetaStar`: `Beta ⊆ Par ⊆ BetaStar`, so their reflexive–transitive closures
   coincide.
2. `cd t` is Takahashi's maximal one-step development of `t`.
3. **Triangle property** (`par_triangle`): if `t ⇒ u` then `u ⇒ cd t`.
4. The triangle gives the **diamond property** of `Par` immediately
   (`par_diamond`): the common reduct of any fork is `cd` of the source.
5. The diamond property lifts to the reflexive–transitive closure via
   `Relation.church_rosser`, yielding `church_rosser_beta`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (H1): β-reduction is confluent, and the cleanest route is parallel
reduction with a *function* `cd` realising the diamond (Takahashi's triangle),
rather than the brittle "diamond by hand" argument.
Experiment: `Par` is defined with reflexive variable/structural rules plus a
β-rule that contracts simultaneously; `cd` is defined by structural recursion
with the redex case `app (lam t) u ↦ subst0 (cd u) (cd t)`.
Analysis: the triangle `Par t u → Par u (cd t)` is the load-bearing lemma; it
needs (a) `Par` to respect `lift` and `subst` (proved via the substitution
algebra in `Syntax.lean`), and (b) inversion of `Par` on `lam`/`app` heads.
Critique: the diamond hypothesis demanded by `Relation.church_rosser` is the
*weak* one (`ReflGen`/`ReflTransGen`); since `Par` is reflexive the full diamond
trivially supplies it.
-- !-- End Lab Notes -- !--
-/

namespace LambdaCalculus

open Lam

/-- **Parallel (Tait–Martin-Löf) reduction**: contracts a set of redexes
simultaneously in one step. -/
inductive Par : Lam → Lam → Prop
  | var (n : ℕ) : Par (var n) (var n)
  | lam {t t' : Lam} : Par t t' → Par (lam t) (lam t')
  | app {a a' b b' : Lam} : Par a a' → Par b b' → Par (app a b) (app a' b')
  | beta {t t' u u' : Lam} : Par t t' → Par u u' →
      Par (app (lam t) u) (subst0 u' t')

/-
Parallel reduction is reflexive.
-/
theorem par_refl (t : Lam) : Par t t := by
  have h_refl : ∀ t : Lam, Par t t := by
    intro t; induction t <;> tauto;
  exact h_refl t

/-
A single β-step is a parallel step.
-/
theorem par_of_beta {t u : Lam} (h : Beta t u) : Par t u := by
  induction h;
  · exact Par.beta ( par_refl _ ) ( par_refl _ );
  · exact Par.app ‹_› ( par_refl _ );
  · exact Par.app ( par_refl _ ) ‹_›;
  · exact Par.lam ‹_›

/-! ### `Par` respects the substitution algebra -/

/-
Parallel reduction commutes with lifting.
-/
theorem par_lift {t t' : Lam} (h : Par t t') (c : ℕ) :
    Par (lift c t) (lift c t') := by
      induction h generalizing c;
      · exact par_refl _;
      · exact Par.lam ( by solve_by_elim );
      · exact Par.app ( by solve_by_elim ) ( by solve_by_elim );
      · rename_i h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄;
        convert Par.beta ( h₃ ( c + 1 ) ) ( h₄ c ) using 1;
        convert lift_subst_ge _ ( Nat.zero_le c ) _ using 1

/-
Parallel reduction is a congruence for substitution.
-/
theorem par_subst {s s' t t' : Lam} (hs : Par s s') (ht : Par t t') (j : ℕ) :
    Par (subst j s t) (subst j s' t') := by
      induction' ht with a a' b b' ha hb ih generalizing j s s';
      · by_cases h : a = j <;> simp_all +decide [ subst ];
        split_ifs <;> [ exact par_refl _; exact par_refl _ ];
      · exact Par.lam ( ha b' ( j + 1 ) |> fun h => by
          exact ha ( par_lift hs 0 ) _ );
      · exact Par.app ( by solve_by_elim ) ( by solve_by_elim );
      · rename_i h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄;
        convert Par.beta _ _ using 1;
        convert subst0_subst _ _ _ _ using 1;
        · exact h₃ ( par_lift hs 0 ) _;
        · exact h₄ hs j

/-- Parallel reduction is a congruence for β-contraction. -/
theorem par_subst0 {u u' t t' : Lam} (hu : Par u u') (ht : Par t t') :
    Par (subst0 u t) (subst0 u' t') :=
  par_subst hu ht 0

/-! ### Complete development and the triangle property -/

/-- Takahashi's **complete development**: contract *all* the redexes currently
present in `t`. -/
def cd : Lam → Lam
  | var n => var n
  | lam t => lam (cd t)
  | app (lam t) u => subst0 (cd u) (cd t)
  | app a b => app (cd a) (cd b)

/-
**Triangle property**: every parallel reduct of `t` parallel-reduces to the
complete development `cd t`.
-/
theorem par_triangle {t u : Lam} (h : Par t u) : Par u (cd t) := by
  induction' t with t ih generalizing u;
  · cases h ; tauto;
  · cases h;
    exact Par.lam ( by solve_by_elim );
  · rename_i a b ih_a ih_b;
    induction a <;> simp_all +decide [ cd ];
    · rcases h with ( _ | _ | _ | _ ) ; tauto;
    · cases h;
      · rename_i a' b' ha hb ih;
        cases' ha with a'' ha'';
        exact Par.beta ( ih_a ( Par.lam ‹_› ) |> fun h => by cases h; assumption ) ( ih_b hb );
      · rename_i k hk₁ hk₂ hk₃;
        exact par_subst0 ( ih_b hk₂ ) ( ih_a ( Par.lam hk₁ ) |> fun h => by cases h; tauto );
    · cases h;
      exact Par.app ( ih_a ‹_› ) ( ih_b ‹_› )

/-- **Diamond property** of parallel reduction. -/
theorem par_diamond {t u v : Lam} (hu : Par t u) (hv : Par t v) :
    ∃ w, Par u w ∧ Par v w :=
  ⟨cd t, par_triangle hu, par_triangle hv⟩

/-! ### From `Par` back to `Beta` -/

/-
`BetaStar` is a congruence under `lam`.
-/
theorem betaStar_lam {t t' : Lam} (h : BetaStar t t') : BetaStar (lam t) (lam t') := by
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := h;
  · constructor;
  · rename_i h₁ h₂;
    exact h₁.lift ( fun x => lam x ) ( fun a b h => Beta.lam h ) |> fun h => h.tail ( Beta.lam h₂ )

/-
`BetaStar` is a congruence in the left argument of an application.
-/
theorem betaStar_appL {a a' : Lam} (h : BetaStar a a') (b : Lam) :
    BetaStar (app a b) (app a' b) := by

`BetaStar` is a congruence in the right argument of an application.

      · constructor;
      · exact Relation.ReflTransGen.tail ‹_› ( Beta.appR _ ‹_› )

A parallel step is realised by a finite β-reduction sequence.

  constructor

    induction h with

theorem church_rosser_beta {t u v : Lam} (h1 : BetaStar t u) (h2 : BetaStar t v) :
    ∃ w, BetaStar u w ∧ BetaStar v w := by
  have h1' : Relation.ReflTransGen Par t u :=

import Logic.LambdaCalculus.Syntax

/-!
# The Church–Rosser theorem for the untyped λ-calculus

We prove confluence (the Church–Rosser property) of β-reduction using the
Tait/Martin-Löf **parallel reduction** `Par` together with Takahashi's
**complete development** `cd`.

## Strategy

1. `Par` reduces several redexes in one step; it sits between `Beta` and
   `BetaStar`: `Beta ⊆ Par ⊆ BetaStar`, so their reflexive–transitive closures
   coincide.
2. `cd t` is Takahashi's maximal one-step development of `t`.
3. **Triangle property** (`par_triangle`): if `t ⇒ u` then `u ⇒ cd t`.
4. The triangle gives the **diamond property** of `Par` immediately
   (`par_diamond`): the common reduct of any fork is `cd` of the source.
5. The diamond property lifts to the reflexive–transitive closure via
   `Relation.church_rosser`, yielding `church_rosser_beta`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (H1): β-reduction is confluent, and the cleanest route is parallel
reduction with a *function* `cd` realising the diamond (Takahashi's triangle),
rather than the brittle "diamond by hand" argument.
Experiment: `Par` is defined with reflexive variable/structural rules plus a
β-rule that contracts simultaneously; `cd` is defined by structural recursion
with the redex case `app (lam t) u ↦ subst0 (cd u) (cd t)`.
Analysis: the triangle `Par t u → Par u (cd t)` is the load-bearing lemma; it
needs (a) `Par` to respect `lift` and `subst` (proved via the substitution
algebra in `Syntax.lean`), and (b) inversion of `Par` on `lam`/`app` heads.
Critique: the diamond hypothesis demanded by `Relation.church_rosser` is the
*weak* one (`ReflGen`/`ReflTransGen`); since `Par` is reflexive the full diamond
trivially supplies it.
-- !-- End Lab Notes -- !--
-/

namespace LambdaCalculus

open Lam

/-- **Parallel (Tait–Martin-Löf) reduction**: contracts a set of redexes
simultaneously in one step. -/
inductive Par : Lam → Lam → Prop
  | var (n : ℕ) : Par (var n) (var n)
  | lam {t t' : Lam} : Par t t' → Par (lam t) (lam t')
  | app {a a' b b' : Lam} : Par a a' → Par b b' → Par (app a b) (app a' b')
  | beta {t t' u u' : Lam} : Par t t' → Par u u' →
      Par (app (lam t) u) (subst0 u' t')

/-
Parallel reduction is reflexive.
-/
theorem par_refl (t : Lam) : Par t t := by
  have h_refl : ∀ t : Lam, Par t t := by
    intro t; induction t <;> tauto;
  exact h_refl t

/-
A single β-step is a parallel step.
-/
theorem par_of_beta {t u : Lam} (h : Beta t u) : Par t u := by
  induction h;
  · exact Par.beta ( par_refl _ ) ( par_refl _ );
  · exact Par.app ‹_› ( par_refl _ );
  · exact Par.app ( par_refl _ ) ‹_›;
  · exact Par.lam ‹_›

/-! ### `Par` respects the substitution algebra -/

/-
Parallel reduction commutes with lifting.
-/
theorem par_lift {t t' : Lam} (h : Par t t') (c : ℕ) :
    Par (lift c t) (lift c t') := by
      induction h generalizing c;
      · exact par_refl _;
      · exact Par.lam ( by solve_by_elim );
      · exact Par.app ( by solve_by_elim ) ( by solve_by_elim );
      · rename_i h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄;
        convert Par.beta ( h₃ ( c + 1 ) ) ( h₄ c ) using 1;
        convert lift_subst_ge _ ( Nat.zero_le c ) _ using 1

/-
Parallel reduction is a congruence for substitution.
-/
theorem par_subst {s s' t t' : Lam} (hs : Par s s') (ht : Par t t') (j : ℕ) :
    Par (subst j s t) (subst j s' t') := by
      induction' ht with a a' b b' ha hb ih generalizing j s s';
      · by_cases h : a = j <;> simp_all +decide [ subst ];
        split_ifs <;> [ exact par_refl _; exact par_refl _ ];
      · exact Par.lam ( ha b' ( j + 1 ) |> fun h => by
          exact ha ( par_lift hs 0 ) _ );
      · exact Par.app ( by solve_by_elim ) ( by solve_by_elim );
      · rename_i h₁ h₂ h₃ h₄;
        convert Par.beta _ _ using 1;
        convert subst0_subst _ _ _ _ using 1;
        · exact h₃ ( par_lift hs 0 ) _;
        · exact h₄ hs j

/-- Parallel reduction is a congruence for β-contraction. -/
theorem par_subst0 {u u' t t' : Lam} (hu : Par u u') (ht : Par t t') :
    Par (subst0 u t) (subst0 u' t') :=
  par_subst hu ht 0

/-! ### Complete development and the triangle property -/

/-- Takahashi's **complete development**: contract *all* the redexes currently
present in `t`. -/
def cd : Lam → Lam
  | var n => var n
  | lam t => lam (cd t)
  | app (lam t) u => subst0 (cd u) (cd t)
  | app a b => app (cd a) (cd b)

/-
**Triangle property**: every parallel reduct of `t` parallel-reduces to the
complete development `cd t`.
-/
theorem par_triangle {t u : Lam} (h : Par t u) : Par u (cd t) := by
  induction' t with t ih generalizing u;
  · cases h ; tauto;
  · cases h;
    exact Par.lam ( by solve_by_elim );
  · rename_i a b ih_a ih_b;
    induction a <;> simp_all +decide [ cd ];
    · rcases h with ( _ | _ | _ | _ ) ; tauto;
    · cases h;
      · rename_i a' b' ha hb ih;
        cases' ha with a'' ha'';
        exact Par.beta ( ih_a ( Par.lam ‹_› ) |> fun h => by cases h; assumption ) ( ih_b hb );
      · rename_i k hk₁ hk₂ hk₃;
        exact par_subst0 ( ih_b hk₂ ) ( ih_a ( Par.lam hk₁ ) |> fun h => by cases h; tauto );
    · cases h;
      exact Par.app ( ih_a ‹_› ) ( ih_b ‹_› )

/-- **Diamond property** of parallel reduction. -/
theorem par_diamond {t u v : Lam} (hu : Par t u) (hv : Par t v) :
    ∃ w, Par u w ∧ Par v w :=
  ⟨cd t, par_triangle hu, par_triangle hv⟩

/-! ### From `Par` back to `Beta` -/

/-
`BetaStar` is a congruence under `lam`.
-/
theorem betaStar_lam {t t' : Lam} (h : BetaStar t t') : BetaStar (lam t) (lam t') := by
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := h;
  · constructor;
  · rename_i h₁ h₂;
    exact h₁.lift ( fun x => lam x ) ( fun a b h => Beta.lam h ) |> fun h => h.tail ( Beta.lam h₂ )

/-
`BetaStar` is a congruence in the left argument of an application.
-/
theorem betaStar_appL {a a' : Lam} (h : BetaStar a a') (b : Lam) :
    BetaStar (app a b) (app a' b) := by
      induction h;
      · constructor;
      · exact Relation.ReflTransGen.tail ‹_› ( Beta.appL _ ‹_› )

/-
`BetaStar` is a congruence in the right argument of an application.
-/
theorem betaStar_appR (a : Lam) {b b' : Lam} (h : BetaStar b b') :
    BetaStar (app a b) (app a b') := by
      induction h;
      · constructor;
      · exact Relation.ReflTransGen.tail ‹_› ( Beta.appR _ ‹_› )

/-
A parallel step is realised by a finite β-reduction sequence.
-/
theorem betaStar_of_par {t u : Lam} (h : Par t u) : BetaStar t u := by
  revert u;
  induction' t with t ih;
  · rintro u ( hu | hu | hu | hu ) ; tauto;
  · intro u hu; cases hu;
    exact betaStar_lam (by solve_by_elim);
  · intro u hu; cases hu;
    · exact Relation.ReflTransGen.trans ( betaStar_appL ( by solve_by_elim ) _ ) ( betaStar_appR _ ( by solve_by_elim ) );
    · rename_i t ht u hu;
      rename_i a ha;
      rename_i b hb;
      convert Relation.ReflTransGen.tail ( Relation.ReflTransGen.trans ( betaStar_appL ( u ( Par.lam ht ) ) b ) ( betaStar_appR _ ( hb hu ) ) ) ( Beta.beta _ _ ) using 1

/-! ### Church–Rosser -/

/-- The reflexive–transitive closures of `Beta` and `Par` coincide. -/
theorem reflTransGen_beta_iff_par (t u : Lam) :
    Relation.ReflTransGen Beta t u ↔ Relation.ReflTransGen Par t u := by
  constructor
  · exact Relation.ReflTransGen.mono (fun _ _ => par_of_beta)
  · intro h
    induction h with
    | refl => exact Relation.ReflTransGen.refl
    | tail _ hbc ih => exact ih.trans (betaStar_of_par hbc)

/-- **Church–Rosser / confluence of β-reduction.**  Any two β-reduction
sequences from a common term can be joined. -/
theorem church_rosser_beta {t u v : Lam} (h1 : BetaStar t u) (h2 : BetaStar t v) :
    ∃ w, BetaStar u w ∧ BetaStar v w := by
  have h1' : Relation.ReflTransGen Par t u :=
    (reflTransGen_beta_iff_par t u).1 h1
  have h2' : Relation.ReflTransGen Par t v :=
    (reflTransGen_beta_iff_par t v).1 h2
  have key : ∀ a b c : Lam, Par a b → Par a c →
      ∃ d, Relation.ReflGen Par b d ∧ Relation.ReflTransGen Par c d := by
    intro a b c hab hac
    obtain ⟨d, hbd, hcd⟩ := par_diamond hab hac
    exact ⟨d, Relation.ReflGen.single hbd, Relation.ReflTransGen.single hcd⟩
  obtain ⟨w, huw, hvw⟩ := Relation.church_rosser key h1' h2'
  exact ⟨w, (reflTransGen_beta_iff_par u w).2 huw, (reflTransGen_beta_iff_par v w).2 hvw⟩

end LambdaCalculus

/-!
# Uniqueness of β-normal forms

A direct consequence of the Church–Rosser theorem
(`LambdaCalculus.church_rosser_beta`): a λ-term has *at most one* β-normal form.
This is the classical corollary that makes "the" normal form of a term a
well-defined notion.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (H2): Confluence collapses the non-determinism of β-reduction at the
level of normal forms — two normal forms reachable from one term must be equal.
Experiment: prove the one-line lemma `betaStar_nf_eq` (a normal form only
reduces to itself) and feed two reductions into `church_rosser_beta`.
Analysis: the only subtlety is that a normal form *can* take zero steps; the
reflexive–transitive closure is inverted with `cases` to extract that a first
step is impossible. Critique: `NormalForm` is the genuinely-empty-redex
predicate (`∀ u, ¬ Beta t u`), so the result is not vacuous — e.g. `Lam.I` and
`Lam.var 0` are bona fide normal forms.
-- !-- End Lab Notes -- !--
-/

namespace LambdaCalculus

open Lam

/-- A normal form β-reduces only to itself. -/
theorem betaStar_nf_eq {u w : Lam} (hu : NormalForm u) (h : BetaStar u w) : u = w := by
  induction h with
  | refl => rfl
  | tail _ hstep _ =>
      -- a single β-step out of a normal form is impossible
      exact absurd hstep (by simp_all [NormalForm])

/-- **Uniqueness of β-normal forms.**  If a term reduces (in any number of steps)
to two normal forms, those normal forms are equal. -/
theorem betaStar_normalForm_unique {t u v : Lam}
    (hu : BetaStar t u) (hv : BetaStar t v)
    (hnu : NormalForm u) (hnv : NormalForm v) : u = v := by
  obtain ⟨w, huw, hvw⟩ := church_rosser_beta hu hv
  have e1 : u = w := betaStar_nf_eq hnu huw
  have e2 : v = w := betaStar_nf_eq hnv hvw
  exact e1.trans e2.symm

/-- `Lam.var n` is a β-normal form (a witness that `NormalForm` is non-vacuous). -/
theorem normalForm_var (n : ℕ) : NormalForm (var n) := by
  intro u h
  cases h

end LambdaCalculus

/-!
# The simply-typed λ-calculus (Curry-style) and subject reduction

We equip the de Bruijn terms of `Syntax.lean` with simple types and a typing
judgement `HasType Γ t T` over a context `Γ : List Ty` (index `0` is the most
recently bound variable, i.e. the head of the list).  The central results are
the structural **weakening** and **substitution** lemmas and, as their payoff,
**subject reduction** (type preservation) for β-reduction and its transitive
closure.

## Main results

* `HasType.weakening`        — inserting a fresh hypothesis preserves typing
  (matched to the de Bruijn shift `lift`).
* `HasType.subst_preserves`  — the substitution lemma (matched to `subst`).
* `HasType.subst0_preserves` — its β-contraction instance (matched to `subst0`).
* `HasType.preservation`     — types are preserved by a β-step.
* `HasType.preservation_star`— types are preserved by `BetaStar`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (H3): For Curry-style STLC over de Bruijn terms, subject reduction
holds and reduces (via the β-case) to a single substitution lemma, which in turn
needs weakening.
Experiment: the load-bearing design choice is the *statement* of the
substitution lemma.  The naive "substituted term typed in the suffix `Γ₂`"
fails, because de Bruijn `subst` re-`lift`s the inserted term under every binder.
The correct invariant is that `s` is typed in `Γ₁ ++ Γ₂` (the context that
*remains* after deletion); then the `lam` case lines up exactly with
`weakening` at cut-point `0`.
Analysis: the var cases are pure `List.getElem?`/`List.length` arithmetic closed
by `omega` after the right `split_ifs`.  Critique: the lemma is not vacuous —
`HasType.lam`/`HasType.app` exhibit genuinely typeable open and closed terms,
and β-reduction really can fire (the β-case of `preservation` is non-trivial).
-- !-- End Lab Notes -- !--
-/

namespace LambdaCalculus

open Lam

/-- Simple types: one base type and function types. -/
inductive Ty : Type where
  | base : Ty
  | arrow : Ty → Ty → Ty
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- The Curry-style typing judgement over a de Bruijn context. -/
inductive HasType : List Ty → Lam → Ty → Prop
  | var {Γ : List Ty} {n : ℕ} {T : Ty} : Γ[n]? = some T → HasType Γ (var n) T
  | lam {Γ : List Ty} {b : Lam} {A B : Ty} :
      HasType (A :: Γ) b B → HasType Γ (lam b) (Ty.arrow A B)
  | app {Γ : List Ty} {f a : Lam} {A B : Ty} :
      HasType Γ f (Ty.arrow A B) → HasType Γ a A → HasType Γ (app f a) B

namespace HasType

/-
**Weakening.**  Inserting a fresh hypothesis `A` at cut-point `|Γ₁|`
preserves typing, with the term shifted by `lift |Γ₁|`.
-/
theorem weakening {Γ₁ Γ₂ : List Ty} {t : Lam} {T : Ty} (A : Ty)
    (h : HasType (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) t T) :
    HasType (Γ₁ ++ A :: Γ₂) (lift Γ₁.length t) T := by
      induction' t with t ih generalizing T Γ₁ Γ₂ A;
      · convert HasType.var ?_;
        rotate_left;
        exact if t < Γ₁.length then t else t + 1;
        · cases h;
          grind +splitImp;
        · unfold lift; aesop;
      · cases h;
        constructor;
        grind +qlia;
      · cases h;
        exact HasType.app ( by aesop ) ( by aesop )

/-- Front-weakening: the `|Γ₁| = 0` instance of `weakening`. -/
theorem weaken0 {Γ : List Ty} {s : Lam} {A B : Ty} (h : HasType Γ s B) :
    HasType (A :: Γ) (lift 0 s) B := by
  have := weakening (Γ₁ := []) (Γ₂ := Γ) A h
  simpa using this

/-
**Substitution lemma.**  If `t` is typeable with a hypothesis `A` at
cut-point `|Γ₁|`, and `s : A` is typeable in the *remaining* context `Γ₁ ++ Γ₂`,
then `subst |Γ₁| s t` is typeable in `Γ₁ ++ Γ₂`.
-/
theorem subst_preserves {Γ₁ Γ₂ : List Ty} {t s : Lam} {A T : Ty}
    (h : HasType (Γ₁ ++ A :: Γ₂) t T) (hs : HasType (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) s A) :
    HasType (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) (subst Γ₁.length s t) T := by
      revert t s;
      intro t s;
      induction' t with t ih generalizing s Γ₁ T;
      · intro h₁ h₂;
        cases h₁;
        simp_all +decide [ List.getElem?_append ];
        split_ifs at * <;> simp_all +decide [ subst ];
        · rw [ if_neg ( by linarith ), if_neg ( by linarith ) ];
          convert HasType.var _;
          grind;
        · split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ List.getElem?_eq_some_iff ];
          · convert HasType.var _ using 1;
            grind;
          · omega;
      · rintro ⟨ B, C, h ⟩ hs;
        apply HasType.lam;
        convert ‹∀ {Γ₁ : List Ty} {T : Ty} {s : Lam}, HasType (Γ₁ ++ A :: Γ₂) ih T → HasType (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) s A → HasType (Γ₁ ++ Γ₂) (subst Γ₁.length s ih) T› ( show HasType ( ( _ :: Γ₁ ) ++ A :: Γ₂ ) ih _ from by simpa [ List.cons_append ] using ‹HasType ( _ :: ( Γ₁ ++ A :: Γ₂ ) ) ih _› ) ( HasType.weaken0 hs ) using 1;
      · rename_i h₁ h₂;
        rintro ( h | h | h ) hs;
        exact HasType.app ( h₁ h hs ) ( h₂ ‹_› hs )

/-- β-contraction instance of the substitution lemma. -/
theorem subst0_preserves {Γ : List Ty} {t s : Lam} {A T : Ty}
    (ht : HasType (A :: Γ) t T) (hs : HasType Γ s A) :
    HasType Γ (subst0 s t) T := by
  have := subst_preserves (Γ₁ := []) (Γ₂ := Γ) (A := A) (by simpa using ht)
    (by simpa using hs)
  simpa [subst0] using this

/-
**Subject reduction** for a single β-step.
-/
theorem preservation {Γ : List Ty} {t u : Lam} {T : Ty}
    (h : HasType Γ t T) (hr : Beta t u) : HasType Γ u T := by
      induction hr generalizing Γ T;
      · cases h;
        rename_i h₁ h₂;
        convert subst0_preserves _ h₁;
        cases h₂ ; tauto;
      · cases h;
        exact HasType.app ( by solve_by_elim ) ( by assumption );
      · cases h;
        exact HasType.app ‹_› ( by solve_by_elim );
      · cases h;
        exact HasType.lam ( by solve_by_elim )

/-- **Subject reduction** for many β-steps. -/
theorem preservation_star {Γ : List Ty} {t u : Lam} {T : Ty}
    (h : HasType Γ t T) (hr : BetaStar t u) : HasType Γ u T := by
  induction hr with
  | refl => exact h
  | tail _ hstep ih => exact preservation ih hstep

end HasType

end LambdaCalculus

import Mathlib

/-!
# Untyped λ-calculus: syntax, substitution and β-reduction (de Bruijn)

This file develops the untyped λ-calculus with de Bruijn indices.  It provides the
basic syntactic apparatus that the rest of the `Logic.LambdaCalculus` development
(confluence, Böhm approximants, …) builds on.

## Main definitions

* `Lam`            — λ-terms with de Bruijn indices.
* `Lam.lift`       — shift of free variables above a cutoff.
* `Lam.subst`      — capture-avoiding substitution for a single variable.
* `Lam.subst0`     — substitution for the outermost bound variable (β-contraction).
* `Beta`           — single-step β-reduction.
* `BetaStar`       — its reflexive–transitive closure.
* `NormalForm`     — a term with no β-redex.
* `Lam.I`, `Lam.Delta`, `Lam.omega` — the combinators `I = λx.x`, `Δ = λx.x x`
  and `Ω = Δ Δ`.

## Main results

The fundamental **substitution algebra** of de Bruijn terms:

* `lift_lift`, `subst_lift_cancel`, `lift_subst_le`, `lift_subst_ge`,
  and the *substitution lemma* `subst_subst`.

These commutation identities are exactly what is needed to make parallel
reduction respect substitution, which in turn powers the Church–Rosser theorem
in `Logic.LambdaCalculus.Confluence`.

-- !-- Lab Notes -- !--
Hypothesis (H0): A small, well-chosen set of lift/subst commutation lemmas
(`lift_lift`, `subst_lift_cancel`, `lift_subst_le`, `lift_subst_ge`,
`subst_subst`) suffices to drive every later substitution obligation.
Experiment: each identity was first validated by exhaustive `#eval` over all
terms of depth ≤ 2 with variable indices < 4 and all cutoffs < 4 before being
proved.  Analysis: the de Bruijn arithmetic is entirely discharged by `omega`
once the term induction is `generalizing` the cutoff/index.  Critique: the two
directions `lift_subst_le`/`lift_subst_ge` are genuinely different (different
index shifts under a binder) and both are needed.
-- !-- End Lab Notes -- !--
-/

namespace LambdaCalculus

/-- λ-terms with de Bruijn indices. -/
inductive Lam : Type where
  | var : ℕ → Lam
  | lam : Lam → Lam
  | app : Lam → Lam → Lam
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

namespace Lam

/-- `lift c t` increments every free variable of `t` whose index is `≥ c`.
This is the de Bruijn shift used when pushing a term under a binder. -/
def lift (c : ℕ) : Lam → Lam
  | var k => if k < c then var k else var (k + 1)
  | lam t => lam (lift (c + 1) t)
  | app a b => app (lift c a) (lift c b)

/-- `subst j s t` substitutes `s` for the variable `j` in `t`, decrementing the
variables strictly above `j` (capture-avoiding via `lift` under binders). -/
def subst (j : ℕ) (s : Lam) : Lam → Lam
  | var k => if k = j then s else if j < k then var (k - 1) else var k
  | lam t => lam (subst (j + 1) (lift 0 s) t)
  | app a b => app (subst j s a) (subst j s b)

/-- β-contraction substitution: replace the outermost bound variable. -/
def subst0 (s t : Lam) : Lam := subst 0 s t

/-- The combinator `I = λx. x`. -/
def I : Lam := lam (var 0)

/-- The self-application `Δ = λx. x x`. -/
def Delta : Lam := lam (app (var 0) (var 0))

/-- The looping term `Ω = Δ Δ = (λx. x x)(λx. x x)`. -/
def omega : Lam := app Delta Delta

/-! ### Substitution algebra -/

/-
Lifts commute (raising the second cutoff when applied innermost).
-/
theorem lift_lift (t : Lam) {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) :
    lift i (lift j t) = lift (j + 1) (lift i t) := by
      induction' t with t ih generalizing i j;
      · grind +locals;
      · simp +decide [ *, Lam.lift ];
      · simp +decide [ *, Lam.lift ]

/-
Substituting at a cutoff that was just created by `lift` is the identity.
-/
theorem subst_lift_cancel (t : Lam) (i : ℕ) (s : Lam) :
    subst i s (lift i t) = t := by
      induction' t with t ih generalizing s i <;> simp +decide [ subst, lift ] at *;
      · split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ subst ]; all_goals grind;
      · convert ‹∀ ( i : ℕ ) ( s : Lam ), subst i s ( lift i ih ) = ih› ( i + 1 ) ( lift 0 s ) using 1;
      · aesop

/-
`lift` pushed through a `subst` when the lift cutoff is `≤` the substituted
variable.
-/
theorem lift_subst_le (t : Lam) {i j : ℕ} (h : i ≤ j) (s : Lam) :
    lift i (subst j s t) = subst (j + 1) (lift i s) (lift i t) := by
      -- We proceed by induction on `t`.
      induction' t with t ih generalizing i j s;
      · simp +decide [ Lam.lift, Lam.subst ];
        split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ Lam.lift, Lam.subst ];
        · linarith;
        · grind;
        · grind;
        · grind;
        · grind;
      · simp +decide [ *, Lam.lift, Lam.subst ];
        rw [ lift_lift s ( Nat.zero_le i ) ];
      · simp_all +decide [ Lam.lift, Lam.subst ]

/-
`lift` pushed through a `subst` when the lift cutoff is `≥` the substituted
variable.
-/
theorem lift_subst_ge (t : Lam) {i j : ℕ} (h : j ≤ i) (s : Lam) :
    lift i (subst j s t) = subst j (lift i s) (lift (i + 1) t) := by
      induction' t with t ih generalizing i j s;
      · simp +decide [ lift, subst ];
        split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ lift, subst ];
        · omega;
        · lia;
        · grind;
        · grind;
      · simp +decide [ *, Lam.lift, Lam.subst ];
        rw [ lift_lift s ( Nat.zero_le i ) ];
      · rename_i a b ih₁ ih₂; exact congr_arg₂ _ ( ih₁ h s ) ( ih₂ h s ) ;

/-
The **substitution lemma** for de Bruijn terms.
-/
theorem subst_subst (e : Lam) {n m : ℕ} (h : n ≤ m) (w v : Lam) :
    subst m w (subst n v e) =
      subst n (subst m w v) (subst (m + 1) (lift n w) e) := by
        induction' e with e ih generalizing n m w v;
        · simp +decide [ Lam.subst ];
          split_ifs <;> simp_all +decide [ Lam.subst ];
          any_goals omega;
          · rw [ subst_lift_cancel ];
          · grind;
          · grind;
          · grind;
        · simp_all +decide [ Lam.subst ];
          grind +suggestions;
        · simp_all +decide [ Lam.subst ]

/-- Special case of `subst_subst` for β-contraction (`n = 0`). -/
theorem subst0_subst (e : Lam) (j : ℕ) (w v : Lam) :
    subst j w (subst0 v e) = subst0 (subst j w v) (subst (j + 1) (lift 0 w) e) := by
  simpa [subst0] using subst_subst e (Nat.zero_le j) w v

end Lam

/-! ### β-reduction -/

open Lam

/-- Single-step β-reduction. -/
inductive Beta : Lam → Lam → Prop
  | beta (t u : Lam) : Beta (app (lam t) u) (subst0 u t)
  | appL {a a' : Lam} (b : Lam) : Beta a a' → Beta (app a b) (app a' b)
  | appR (a : Lam) {b b' : Lam} : Beta b b' → Beta (app a b) (app a b')
  | lam {t t' : Lam} : Beta t t' → Beta (lam t) (lam t')

/-- Multi-step β-reduction: the reflexive–transitive closure of `Beta`. -/
def BetaStar : Lam → Lam → Prop := Relation.ReflTransGen Beta

/-- A term is in normal form when no β-step applies. -/
def NormalForm (t : Lam) : Prop := ∀ u, ¬ Beta t u

end LambdaCalculus
